title: P50-family MTP depth: the pretraining-only DeepSeek-style MTP module gets two Peri-LN blocks instead of one (same t+2 target, weight 0.3, dropped at handoff) on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (9,557,760 params, handoff model unchanged)
description: Idea ID: P50 family (pretraining objectives on the same examples; the 136-fable MTP lane). pretrain.py is 153-claude's except MTP_DEPTH = 2: the MTP module's input projection is followed by two Peri-LN blocks in sequence instead of one before the shared ln_f/head predicts token t+2; the auxiliary weight (0.3), target, input and handoff are unchanged and the handed-off model is byte-for-byte the same architecture as 153. This is a mechanism test of WHY MTP won (136: +11.7): its follow-ups changed the target or the weight (138 t+3 -17, 141 no true-next-token input -21, 142 deep supervision -26, 143 weight schedule -3, 144 weight 0.6 -27) and all lost, so the surviving reading is that the trunk gains from being the lower part of a deeper network during pretraining (extra pretraining-only depth whose gradient flows into h_t), which the 10M cap does not count; if that is the mechanism, a deeper auxiliary module should help RL more, at the cost of ~11% fewer steps (bench 10.24 vs 11.53 steps/s). Concurrent registrations 163-claude (repeat 6-line records) and 163-fable3 (prompt-token loss) are different ideas.
hypothesis: Two candidate mechanisms for the 136 MTP keep, which its follow-ups could not separate: (a) the t+2 target itself forces h_t to encode the coming step (target-driven); (b) the extra pretraining-only block makes the trunk the bottom of a 7-block network whose top block is discarded, so h_t is shaped by a richer readout than the linear head and by gradients that passed through one more attention/MLP block (depth-driven; a form of 'train deep, hand off shallow'). Changing only the module depth keeps (a) fixed and doubles (b): the MTP readout of h_t becomes a 2-block network. Under (b) the trunk representation should transfer better to expert iteration (the RL stage fine-tunes only the 6-block trunk, so any gain must be in h), showing up as a higher eval/round-4 transfer ratio or a better round-1 sampler; under (a) alone the change is neutral apart from the step loss and the deeper module absorbing more of the t+2 work itself (it can do more of the lookahead internally, so h_t is pushed LESS to carry it), which would make it a small loss. Cost: one more block per step in pretraining (~1/8 of block compute plus its Muon work), predicted ~11% fewer steps (bench 617 steps in 60 s vs 153's probe 692), still ~3.5 epochs, past the ~3-epoch point where 148 found extra steps wasted, so the step loss should cost little.
expected_delta: -35 to +35 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +5; keep needs > 687.00 (153-claude: 676/700/685). Mechanism predictions: pretraining steps 3,800-4,300 per seed (153: 4540/4479/4489; bench 10.24 steps/s in the first 60 s vs 153's 11.53 probe, -11%), ~3.4-3.8 epochs; handoff n_params 9,557,760 exactly; peak memory ~7.4 GB (bench). mtp_loss at 300 s about equal to the main train loss as in 136-153 (the t+2 target is as easy as t+1 here), possibly slightly lower (0.04-0.06) with the deeper module; final main val loss 0.080-0.095 (153: 0.088/0.087/0.089), held-out greedy after pretraining 0.955-0.975 (153: 0.9675/0.967/0.968). Under mechanism (b): round-1 RL targets solved 700-850 (153: 766/747/694), round-4 RL-solved 1,150-1,210 (153: 1157/1168/1191), eval/round-4 transfer ratio >= 0.585 (153: 0.584/0.599/0.575). RL sampling 200-290 samples/s (handoff model unchanged), totals 1,650-1,900 s. Falsifiers: mean steps < 3,600 (the extra block cost more than measured), round-1 targets solved < 600 on two seeds (the deeper module made a worse sampler), or a metric below 660 (mechanism (b) rejected: pretraining-only depth does not transfer).

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude except width; PeriLNBlock now replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280 (same as 151's 4*320)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: none in the handed-off model vs 153-claude (ALiBiGPT, six Peri-LN blocks, D 384, 8 heads of 48 with the hybrid ALiBi/NoPE slope table, d_ff 1280, 9,557,760 params). The only change is the pretraining-only MTP module: MTP_DEPTH = 2, i.e. its input proj (384, 768) is followed by TWO Peri-LN blocks (ModuleList) applied in sequence instead of one, before the model's own ln_f/head predicts token t+2. Same target (t+2), same weight 0.3, same input [ln(h_t); ln(emb(x_{t+1}))], same causal ALiBi bias slice; the module is never registered on the model and is dropped at handoff.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107, identical to 153; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported 9,557,760). MTP module (pretraining only, dropped at handoff): 3,454,720 = 153's 1,875,584 + one more Peri-LN block 1,579,136; pretraining trains 13,012,480 in total. The harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use.
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.5e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's nine 2D matrices (two blocks x (qkv split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 9 matrices: 34 Muon matrices (153: 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters (both blocks), before both optimizers (unchanged rule)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the two-block MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's input proj (384,768) and two blocks' qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2: 34 Muon matrices during pretraining (CPU check: 34); the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151/153: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter (both MTP blocks) with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 695 steps in 60.3 s = 11.53 steps/s (148-fable's shape: 13.2), peak 7.42 GB, n_params 9,557,760, sampling 179 samples/s (148: 186)

mtp.target: token t+2 at proof positions (mask m[:, 2:]), through the model's own ln_f/head
mtp.input: proj(cat(ln_h(h_t), ln_e(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, then block 1 then block 2 (each a PeriLNBlock(384, 8), d_ff 1280, hybrid ALiBi/NoPE bias slice [..., :-1, :-1])
mtp.change: 153/136: one block. Here: two blocks in sequence. Weight, target, input and handoff unchanged.
mtp.cpu_check: main loss identical to the fork's loss_on (4.680822 both); gradients reach every trunk parameter and every parameter of both MTP blocks; perturbing x[7] changes MTP outputs only at positions >= 6 (position 6 predicts x[8] and legitimately reads emb(x[7]); position 5, which predicts x[7], is unchanged: no leakage)
mtp.stats: mtp_depth is written into the pretrain stats; mtp_loss per curve point unchanged
